title: SRE light handoff brief — Dec 03 2029
summary: Concise end-of-week handoff for the overnight SRE shift. Covers two small incidents (cached-model-ttl evaporation, region-y coldstart spike), current SLO snapshot, actions for next 24h, and lightweight runbook edits. Quick check for canary traffic routing config and autoscale thresholds.
body:
Purpose
This is a compact handoff for the SRE night shift (Dec 3 -> Dec 4, 2029). Use this to get context fast: what happened, what to watch, and immediate actions. Not exhaustive — see linked artifacts for full incident pages and runbook diffs.

Highlights since last handoff
- Incident A (low severity): cache TTL regression for hosted-api model-prefix caching caused increased tokens-per-request for a subset of keys between 01:42–02:15 UTC. Root cause: config rollback during a brief console deploy reverted prefix-TTL from 12h to 5m. Impact: 4% increase in token egress for dev and internal test tenants; latency unaffected. Mitigation: manual TTL patch at 02:20, cache warm started over 20 minutes. Follow-up: add deploy-time TTL verification check (JIRA-SRE-4521).
- Incident B (medium-low): region-y coldstart surge at 04:07 UTC after a routine canary flip. Symptom: p95 generation latency in region-y jumped from 120ms to 980ms for ~8 minutes; autoscale was triggered but warmup delay plus kernel load led to degraded p95. Impact: brief degradation for ~0.4% of requests. Mitigation: automatic fallback to region-x for canary-routes at 04:14. Action: audit canary traffic split and add 30s buffer for allocation (CON-9876).
- Ongoing: cfg-sync alerts intermittently firing for private-deploy control-plane (two alerts in last 72h). No customer-facing impact collected yet; ops team monitoring.

SLO snapshot (as of 2029-12-03 18:00 UTC)
- Hosted API availability: 99.98% (30d rolling) — within target 99.95% SLA. No action.
- Gen p95 latency (global): 135ms (7d median) — within SLO but region-y drifted to 220ms. Watchlist: region-y infra rebuild scheduled tonight.
- Error rate (4xx+5xx): 0.12% (24h) — slight uptick, correlated to malformed requests from an internal integration. Follow-up: customer-success flagged integration owner; see linked ticket.

Runbook & tooling notes
- Short patch applied to cache-runbook: added 'verify-prefix-ttl' step post-deploy. PR merged to ops-runbooks (#312). Please confirm step exists in practice by running the 'ttl-check' script on next deploy to staging.
- Canary orchestration: add an allocation buffer for coldstart-sensitive models (30s spin time). Temporary mitigation done via routing policy that keeps 10% extra capacity warm; need engineering review for permanent solution.

On-call handoff items (priority order)
1) Watch cache-ttl alert (TTL_LOW_THRESHOLD): if seen, follow the 'verify-prefix-ttl' flow — patch in console -> run warmstart -> monitor token-ejection metric. Escalate to Marcus if patch fails.
2) Region-y coldstart p95: if p95 > 500ms for >10m, trigger failover to region-x for affected canary route and post an incident stub. Notify product-hosted-api.
3) cfg-sync spikes: track frequency; if >3 within 24h, open an incident and roll back the last control-plane config change.
4) Malformed request spike source: reach out to integration owner (CS pinged) and block-by-thumb rule if reproducible.

Action items and owners
- Priya: Draft TTL preflight test and add to CI (due: 2029-12-06).
- Marcus: Engineering deep dive on region-y coldstart pattern (due: 2029-12-10).
- Rosa: Monitor cfg-sync and collect logs for next 48h (in progress).
- Ethan: Confirm canary routing policy change is reversible and document rollback (due: 2029-12-05).

Notes for night shift
- Short checklist for incoming oncall: (1) glance SLO dashboard (p95, errors), (2) open 'ops-runbooks/ttl-check' script, (3) ensure region-y warm capacity >= baseline, (4) confirm no new deploys are scheduled for the first 2h.
- Pager expectation: TTL_LOW_THRESHOLD page -> 20 min to initial mitigation; region-y p95 page -> 10 min to initial mitigation and failover if unresolved for 10m.

Follow-ups and open questions
- Should we make the canary buffer a dynamic percent based on traffic (CON-9876)? Pros: cost saver at low traffic; cons: complexity in autoscaler logic. Need product input.
- Is the TTL verification step something platform pipelines can run automatically pre-deploy rather than manual post-patch? Engineering feasibility assessment pending.

Useful links
- Full incident A page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/cache-ttl-2029-12-03
- Region-y coldstart analysis draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/region-y-coldstart-draft
- PR (runbook): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/312
- JIRA-SRE-4521: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-4521

Quick sign-off
- Handoff prepared by: Priya Malhotra (eng-sre)
- Last verification: 2029-12-04 02:30 UTC by Marcus Lee (confirmed TTL patch applied and canary routing reverted to baseline)

TL;DR: Two small incidents this window (cache TTL regression and short region coldstart spike). SLOs nominal but watch region-y latency and cfg-sync alerts. Short-term mitigations applied; next steps are preflight TTL checks and a region-y coldstart engineering review.
